tasks.short: Supervise engineers on network design and implementation

steps.what: Send this week's design status
Place open designs on the task board
Read the design before the review
Review the design with the engineer
File the signed design review note
Implement the signed network design

tasks.design: Network engineers send site, task id, design version and due date. A {PROJECT} board shows only late or unsigned designs. The network architect still holds the review and signs one note. The engineer may implement only that signed note, which is filed in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status lived in mail and in the room, so a list could not tell a late task from a design the architect had not accepted.
tasks.enabler_now: A task id, a site and a due date can sit on one record, so lateness is a date comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Coaching a weak design, and deciding what may be implemented, still happen in the review.
tasks.human_edge: The architect accepts or sends back a design and names who may implement it.

ambition.what: Review each open design every week, not only at the project gate

tasks.altitude: Less time chasing status, the same time in the review. The architect can refuse an implementation that has no signed note.

reach.task: Implement only the design version named in the review note
reach.learn: Which designs were signed this week and which were sent back

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this supervision is a weekly review of people and designs. Only the status chase is a date comparison.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so the engineer implements from the signed note and an unattended change is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when the signed review note is filed. The engineer does the implementation.
Input contract: task id, site, design version, owner, due date. Producer is the network engineer. If the mail has no task id, the architect types one and marks the row manual.

The meeting prior fits this task. About half the time is the review and is not treated as saved. Use the project board's own filters before custom code. The board lists tasks, not a record of how staff spend their day.
unknowns: Who may sign a design when the architect is absent.
Whether engineers may change production outside a change window.
research_questions: What share of design tasks has no owner or no due date?
How often is a design sent back more than once?

already_counted.description: Architect's coaching time in the design review
Architect still reads the design itself

incremental.description: Adjust the board filters when a new site type appears
Engineers resubmit a status that has no task id

approvals.approved_version: design review note signed in this meeting
the same signed design review note

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes designs still arrive as mail without a task id, so the board stays thin and the review is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test new hardware or software for interoperability

steps.what: Send the product build and interfaces
Write pass rules for this product version
Run interoperability tests on the rack
Read counters from the test rack
Draft the interoperability result note

loop.output: note that cites row ids only
loop.check: Every pass or fail sentence cites a measured row id
loop.stop: One draft; drop any sentence with no row id
loop.why_not_simpler: A brochure phrase does not match a counter by a fixed table

steps.what: Sign pass, fail, or another test
File the signed test result

tasks.design: The vendor engineer sends a product version and its interface list on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. The architect writes pass rules, runs the tests on the rack, and reads counters in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded note in {DOCS} may cite only measured rows. The architect signs pass, fail, or another test, and only that result is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product claims arrived as brochures and the measurements sat in a notebook, so a note could not show which row a sentence used.
tasks.enabler_now: A product version and a row id can be stored with each counter reading.
tasks.still_hard: Whether two products really work together on this firm's traffic is still a lab judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The architect sets the pass rules and decides pass, fail, or another test.

ambition.what: Record a pass or fail when the product version changes, not only at the yearly refresh

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting result rows. The architect can refuse a result that cites no measurement, and nothing moves from the rack to the live network in this task.

reach.task: Answer a fail against the signed result
reach.learn: Which product version failed and which row was cited

evidence.claim: Lab tests of new network products in a mid-size firm are yearly and hands-on. Only repeated measurements can be checked against a pass rule.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so a pass or fail is taken from a measured row, not from a filled column.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a lab result is not pushed onto the live network.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a filed pass or fail. Changing production is a later task.

Input contract: product version, interface name, row id, counter, expected value. Producer is the vendor engineer for the claim list, and the rack for the rows. A claim with no row id is dropped from the note.
Test native counter export before custom code. The in-person prior fits the rack. Screen time is the counter check during that same test.
unknowns: Which products expose counters versus a front panel only.
Who may sign a result when the architect is away.
research_questions: What share of tested products is a new version of one already failed?
How often is the first result a retest?

already_counted.description: Architect's time on the rack stays in the test
Architect edits a weak result note before signing

incremental.description: Add a pass rule when a new interface type is tested
Vendor engineer resends a pack that has no version

approvals.approved_version: test result signed for this product version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most products have no measured row the note can cite, so the architect still writes the result by hand. The rack time and the pass or fail are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Estimate time and materials for network projects

steps.what: Send scope lines with task ids
Pull standard hours and part counts
Draft the time and materials estimate

loop.output: estimate lines citing a task id and a rate id
loop.check: Every hour figure equals the rate row times the quantity
loop.stop: Leave the line blank if the task id has no rate row
loop.why_not_simpler: Hours for unfamiliar work are not a fixed multiplication

steps.what: Judge hours that have no rate
Check the estimate total
File the signed estimate version

tasks.design: The project controller sends task id, site, quantity and work type on a {PROJECT} form. Standard hours and part counts come from rate rows in the {SPREADSHEET}. A bounded draft writes only the lines that match a rate. The architect judges the rest and signs the estimate version in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scope arrived as prose and rates lived in old workbooks, so a draft could not tell a standard line from a guess.
tasks.enabler_now: A task id can join a scope line to a rate row and a part count.
tasks.still_hard: Work the firm has not done before has no honest rate.
tasks.human_edge: The architect sets the hours for unrated work and signs the estimate.

ambition.what: Re-estimate when a scope line changes, not only at project start

tasks.altitude: Rated lines stop being recopied. The architect keeps the unrated lines and can refuse an estimate that invents an hour.

reach.task: Hold the budget to the signed estimate version
reach.learn: Which lines used a rate and which the architect judged

evidence.claim: Estimates in a mid-size firm are lines of hours and parts. Repeated work has a rate. New work does not.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so hour figures come from rate rows, not from a filled column.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed estimate. Buying the parts is a later purchasing task.
Input contract: task id, site, work type, quantity, rate id, part id. Producer is the project controller. A line with no task id is returned, not estimated.
Use the workbook's own lookup before custom code. The meeting prior fits the judgement of unrated work, not the rate lookup. Rates are not a record of a named person's speed.
unknowns: Which work types have a rate the firm still trusts.
Who may sign an estimate above a given total.
research_questions: What share of scope lines has no rate id?
How often does the signed total change after the first estimate?

already_counted.description: Architect corrects draft lines that used the wrong rate

incremental.description: Add a rate row when a new work type repeats
Project controller resubmits lines with no task id

approvals.approved_version: estimate version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes half the scope lines have no rate row, so the draft stays short and the judgement meeting is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design and deliver product skills sessions

steps.what: Name who must attend the session
Draft the session handout

loop.input: signed product note and handout sections
loop.output: steps that each cite a feature id
loop.check: Every step cites a feature id on the signed product note
loop.stop: One draft; drop any step with no feature id
loop.why_not_simpler: The order of a lesson is not a fixed mail-merge

steps.what: Sign the handout version
Book the room and the roster
Deliver the product skills session
Attend the skills session

tasks.design: A service owner names the audience, the product version and the skill on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded handout in {DOCS} may cite only features on the signed product note. The architect signs that handout version, books the roster on the {CALENDAR}, and delivers the session. The room is not replaced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts were rewritten from memory, and the roster lived in mail, so two sessions could teach different steps.
tasks.enabler_now: A feature id on the signed product note can be checked against each handout step.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching a room, and answering the question that was not on the handout, stays with the architect.
tasks.human_edge: The architect signs what may be taught and delivers the session.

ambition.what: Supplier engineers get the same signed handout as staff

tasks.altitude: Less time rebuilding the handout. The architect keeps the room and can refuse to teach from an unsigned draft.

reach.task: Follow the signed handout in the session
reach.learn: Which handout version was signed and which features it cites

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm the session in the room is the task. A handout can be checked against a feature list. The teaching cannot.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so handout steps cite a feature id rather than a filled column.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when the session is delivered from a signed handout. A supplier session uses the same steps with the vendor engineer as the attendee.

Input contract: product version, feature id, audience, site, session date. Producer of the audience is the service owner. Producer of the feature list is the signed product note. A step with no feature id is dropped.
Use the calendar's own roster before custom code. Attendance is a headcount for the roster, not a score of staff. The meeting prior fits the delivery and is not treated as saved.
unknowns: Whether small sites can spare people for a shared session.
Who delivers the session when the architect is away.
research_questions: What share of sessions still uses an unsigned handout?
How often is the same product taught differently at two sites?

already_counted.description: Architect still edits the handout before signing
Delivery time in the room stays with the architect

incremental.description: Revise the handout when the signed product note gains a feature
Service owners correct a request that has no audience

approvals.approved_version: handout version signed before this session

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes each session still needs a fresh handout and a full delivery. Only the roster booking is lighter, and the room time is not saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The architect keeps the design review, the lab rack and the training room, and stops chasing status, retyping test rows and rebuilding estimate lines.
reach: Network engineers get a signed review note instead of a corridor instruction.
Vendor engineers get a pass or fail tied to one product version.
Project controllers get hour lines that each cite a task id.
System users and supplier engineers get one signed handout before the session.
skills_to_grow: Record a design review as a decision with an owner and a date.
Tie a lab result to a product version and a pass rule.
Separate a standard hour line from work that has no rate.
Deliver the session, and file only the handout version.
role.ambitious_version: Each open design has a weekly signed note, each product version has a pass or fail, and each session uses the same handout.
